info.title: Account Graph HTTP API
info.description: Supply your graph’s HTTPS address. Each /v1 call takes one JSON object. Requests may contain up to 1,000,000 bytes and 32 levels of nesting. A domain refusal is part of the HTTP 200 answer. The unversioned reviewer routes serve the bundled screen.

servers.description: The origin of your graph server.

post.summary: Record up to 100 entries in order
post.description: A service token can record any entry. A reviewer can record only their own statements about a call or a lead, each signed with the token owner’s name: who a call was with, that a caller was reached or was not, and that a call or a text is or is not from a lead.

post.summary: Report a visit or event, or request a token, number or code
post.description: Omit kind for a visit. carry needs LINK_SECRET, number needs POOL_NUMBERS and text_code needs TEXT_CODES. The tag supplies a device on every request. When configured, the server can also supply a device from its cookie. Across origins, send JSON as text/plain, including when sending cookies. An OPTIONS preflight from an allowed origin receives 405.

bearerAuth.description: Use the service token or a reviewer token with access to the call.

closed.description: Of them, those that began while you were closed. Null when your hours are not known.

reported.description: Of those, how many a system of yours reported, and no call shows.

calledAgain.description: Missed and voicemail calls whose caller rang again and got through.

notLeads.description: Calls said to be no lead. They are in none of the counts above.

hidden.description: Missed and voicemail calls from a hidden number, which cannot be returned.

cells.description: Counts by the hour a call began and the day of the week, Monday 1 to Sunday 7, in the time zone asked for. Hours with no calls are left out.

visitor.description: Tied to the one visitor who tapped the number.

channel.description: Filed under the channel its number is published on, and nothing more.

noResult.description: With no result, whatever the rest: waiting or unknown.

coverage.description: How calls to you were placed: each call is in exactly one of the first three.

returnedWithin.description: Half of the returned calls were returned within this many milliseconds. Null when none was.

Change.description: A subject whose cluster moved. `from` is undefined for a subject not seen before.

a.description: Who was asked about, and who they may be against: another that was asked about, or somebody on record.

how.description:
`recorded` the two were separated. `same` one of their clusters holds somebody separated from somebody in the other's.
`possible` the same, of someone either is only related to, so a person has to look.

rests.description: The separated pair it rests on.

Conflict.description: Two that are kept apart, or may be the same as two who are, of those asked about.

adUserData.description: Their data may be sent to an ad platform to measure ads.

adPersonalization.description: Their data may be used to personalize ads.

Consent.description: What a person agreed to. Both are about advertising; neither affects fraud checks.

Decided.description: An Outcome whose "no" carries what that reason needs.

least.description: A row of fewer people than this is not shown, because one person more or less would move it too far.

first.description: Of the groups by what their first call was like.

returned.description: Of the group by whether a miss was returned. `through`: they got through on their own before the landmark, so whether they were rung back says nothing.

excluded.description: People left out, and why, apart for the two questions, because someone may count for one and not for the other.

Followed.description:
What followed calls, not what they caused. People choose whether to call,
how long to talk and whether to call again, and whoever rings them back
chooses whom to ring, so a difference between two rows is not an effect.

state.description:
`open` nobody has spoken to the caller since. `returned` you rang back
and they answered, or a system of yours says they were reached. `called again` they called again and got through.
`hidden` they hid their number, so it cannot be returned.

by.description: The call that closed it, or that a return was reported for, and how long after the miss that was, in milliseconds.

reported.description: A system of yours reported the return, and no call shows it.

reporter.description: Who signed that report, in a person's history, where the report was signed.

attempts.description: How often you rang and nothing says they answered, before it was closed.

FollowUp.description: What became of a call no one answered.

Outcome.description: A domain "no" is a value, never an exception.

rows.description: Highest cost first, then highest value.

missed.description: Calls no one answered, by result, credited the way outcomes are. They are never outcomes.

notLeads.description: Outcomes and calls said to be no lead, credited the same way. They are in no other number here.

stages.description: Outcomes credited to this row, per step, how many people they are, and how long after their arrival they came.

outcomes.description: Outcomes credited to this row, all steps together.

people.description: How many people those outcomes are, whatever accounts they used. A renewal is a second outcome and not a second person.

valueChange.description: What those outcomes were first worth and are worth now.

costDays.description: How many days of the period, up to today, have cost data for this campaign, and how many have none.

insufficientData.description: Fewer than half of the days have cost data, which is too few to say what anything cost. Never so for spend on no campaign, nor for a campaign with no paid arrival and no cost at all. On the total, every campaign that would count is so.

costPerOutcome.description:
The cost over the outcomes credited to this campaign on the days that
have cost data. Null when there is no cost, no such outcome, or too few days.

returnOnCost.description: The value of those outcomes over the same cost. Null for the same reasons, or when they are worth nothing.

reported.description: What the platform says it brought. Absent where it said nothing. On the total, over the rows that have one.

breakdown.description: The same outcomes by the dimension asked for. Costs are not split. A campaign is charged whole.

days.description: Over how many days of the period costs could have been recorded, which are those up to today.

incomplete.description:
Set when part of the period is too recent for its arrivals to have done
all they will. `after` is the last day that has had its time, and `days`
how long that is: 95 in 100 outcomes of the slowest step come within it.

first.description: Of outcomes whose first value is known. `firstUnknown` counts the others, which are in none of this sum.

now.description: What all of them are worth now, net of the two below.

refunded.description: Of what they were worth, how much was given back, and how much will not come, where a change of value said so.

zeroed.description: How many were worth something once and are worth nothing now.

months.description: The outcomes of the period by the month they were first recorded in, `YYYY-MM`, oldest first. Those from before there was a history are under `(not set)`.

excluded.description: Campaigns with cost data on too few days, left out of the total's cost per outcome and return.

by.description: The dimension the rows are broken down by, when one was asked for.

per.description: The one step `costPerOutcome` counts, when one was asked for. The return still sets all value against the cost.

dimensions.description: The dimensions something in these days was recorded under, for choosing one.

currencies.description: Every currency the costs and outcomes named. More than one means the sums mix currencies.

subjects.description: The subjects in the order value moved, starting with the one asked about. The last pays the first.

amount.description: The least that moved along any step, which is the most that could have gone all the way round.

tied.description: How many of the others are in the same cluster as the first. A ring among one person's accounts is the clearest sign.

Ring.description: Value that left a subject and came back to it through others: A paid B, B paid C, C paid A.

by.description: The text or call that replied, and which of the two it was.

delay.description: From the text to the reply, in milliseconds.

TextReply.description: What became of a text to you. `stopped` the sender asked for no more texts before anyone replied.

how.description: `self` it is the subject asked about. `cluster` the graph treats the two as one person. `linked` they are linked strongly enough to be credited, and a cut keeps them in two clusters.

score.description: Strength of the best chain of links: from the subject asked about inside its cluster, and from the nearest of the cluster to anybody else. Null when no chain is left.

via.description: The subjects that chain passes through, starting at the one it begins from.

kinds.description: The kinds of identifier the chain's last link rests on, strongest first.

Tie.description: Why something a subject did belongs to the person asked about.

At.description: Epoch milliseconds, an integer. Always given by the caller. Never defaulted.

entries.description: 1 to 100. One at a time, in order, one transaction each. A later entry sees what an earlier one committed, and one refusal undoes nothing.

history.description: The entries are a load of the past. They are recorded and counted as any others, and nothing is sent to an ad platform for them, now or later.

Keyed.description: `key` is yours, 1 to 200 characters, and unique within its `type`. The graph never mints one. A `conversion` key may not begin with `call:`, `text:` or `page:`.

subject.description: At most 512 UTF-8 bytes, with no surrounding whitespace.

createdAt.description: At most one day after at. Only a firm record may have a creation date.

facts.description: At least one, unless somebody speaks for them.

message.description: What they wrote, such as the message of a form. Kept for a while as a copy to read back with `lookup` `messages`, and never read by matching. Up to 4,000 characters are kept.

speaker.description: Somebody else who told this, such as a parent: their own browser, number or email. What is theirs is not written on the subject, and neither is joined to the other.

Speaker.description: Whoever speaks for a subject. One without a device or a phone is not used, and a note says so.

identifiers.description: Already `kind:value`: `hardware:…`, `passkey:…`, `payment:…`. Kinds the graph writes itself are refused. See KIND_RESERVED.

Facts.description: Plain facts. The graph normalizes, checks and hashes them. At least one.

subject.description: At most 512 UTF-8 bytes, with no surrounding whitespace.

CostEntry.description: `at` is when the platform was read. Per row, the newest `at` stands. No subject.

subject.description: At most 512 UTF-8 bytes, with no surrounding whitespace.

actions.description: What it counts as on each platform. Left out, the stage's own.

userAgent.description: The actual converting browser's HTTP user agent, only for consented Meta website conversions with capture enabled.

PaymentEntry.description: May come before its conversion. Once there is one, the conversion is worth what was paid, and restatements of value are refused with PAID.

code.description: The code the caller read out or entered, from the page they saw. Pages are given codes where the server has `textCodes` on. Never kept.

caller.description: What the phone company says of an inbound caller: the name on its caller ID, and the place the number is from. Kept on the record of the number for staff to read. Never used to match, because it is often the account holder or a carrier's placeholder.

by.description: Who says so. A reviewer signs their own name, and a named service its own.

subject.description: At most 512 UTF-8 bytes, with no surrounding whitespace.

seen.description: The key of the party statement the writer saw, or null if none stood. Omit to write unconditionally.

CallUpdateEntry.description: May come before its call. `at` is when it was said. The newest by (`at`, `key`) stands, whatever order they arrive in.

text.description: Read for a code and for STOP. An inbound text's words are also kept for a while as a copy to read back with `lookup` `messages`. Up to 4,000 characters are kept.

subject.description: At most 512 UTF-8 bytes, with no surrounding whitespace.

LinkEntry.description: The same entry always gives the same URL.

from.description: At most 512 UTF-8 bytes, with no surrounding whitespace.

to.description: At most 512 UTF-8 bytes, with no surrounding whitespace.

adPersonalization.description: Their data may be used to personalize ads.

Told.description: `duplicate`: the key was recorded before, and the rest says how it stands now. `stands`: false when something newer already does.

adUserData.description: Their data may be sent to an ad platform to measure ads.

adPersonalization.description: Their data may be used to personalize ads.

Delivery.description: What a caller may know of an outbox job. No keys, attempts, rev or due.

RecordRefusal.description: None of these is kept with the key. Fix what was wrong and send the same key again.

party.description: The current party statement, even if the phone report has yet to arrive. A reviewer token is not told whom a call was not with.

pair.description: Whether two records are one person now, and what they share. `link` is null where they share nothing that counts.

unconfirmed.description: What they share would join them, and nothing confirms that they are one person. See the policy's `records`.

Match.description: Why is said by kind. No identifier leaves the graph, because most are hashes of an email or a phone.

adUserData.description: Their data may be sent to an ad platform to measure ads.

adPersonalization.description: Their data may be used to personalize ads.

possible.description: The strongest arrival, where none is strong enough to credit.

custom.description: Parameters of your own that the landing address carried.

CampaignCredit.description: A visitor known only through a call can supply its campaign. Their arrival stays private.

timeZone.description: A named time zone, such as America/Chicago.

Window.description: An inclusive range of calendar days. The first day must be on or before the last.

step.description: Null for missed and not returned.

after.description: `cursor` of the last page you acted on. Null to start. It is opaque, because it names this database's history as well as a place in it.

UnrecognizedEvent.description: From a newer server. Keep it, and move on.

prefix.description: Subjects this source writes start with it and a colon. Defaults to `lead:<name>`.

trustSubjects.description: Lets the mapped `subject` name any record, not only one under the prefix. Only for a sender trusted with every record.

updates.description: Adds the new details of a lead posted again under its ID. Only safe when the vendor assigns the ID, never when a visitor can edit it.

conversions.description: For a payment source, required: the conversion key prefixes it may pay, such as `lead:intake` for `lead:intake:I28`.

maxAmount.description: For a payment source, required: the most it may pay one conversion, over all its payments together.
